title: Rework auth header contracts: consolidate scoped tokens, prefetch-nonce, and CORS for streaming/tooling compatibility
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We saw multiple customer and internal integration bugs where streaming endpoints and tool/function-calling flows failed preflight or dropped scoped credentials. Root causes: (1) inconsistent header names across runtime/OpenAI-compat/proxy layers, (2) prefetch nonce header being treated inconsistently by the CDN/proxy, (3) CORS preflight not exposing the minimal set of headers required for SSE and tool negotiation, and (4) token-scheme ambiguity (Bearer vs RedwoodScope) causing silent fallbacks and audit gaps. This PR consolidates the header contract across runtime, openai-compat shim, SDKs and docs to reduce surface area for future regressions and make the streaming/tooling path robust. Changes in this PR: - Introduces a single canonical header set: Authorization (Bearer | RedwoodScope), X-Redwood-Project, X-Redwood-Org, X-Redwood-Scope (optional), X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce (for preflight signalling), X-Redwood-Sig (optional signed-request header). Servers now prefer Authorization for auth decisions but accept X-Redwood-Project keys as fallback for backwards compatibility. - Normalizes prefetch flow: the prefetch nonce header was renamed to X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce and added to Access-Control-Allow-Headers and Access-Control-Expose-Headers for streaming endpoints. The runtime now echoes the nonce on preflight to make CDN/proxy caching policies stable. - OpenAI compatibility mapping: the shim will map OpenAI-typical headers to Redwood equivalents: OpenAI-Organization -> X-Redwood-Org, and supports both 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' as well as 'Authorization: RedwoodScope <token>'. When a RedwoodScope token is used, the runtime enforces scope checks on tool/function calls and emits structured audit markers. - Signed requests: we accept a legacy X-Redwood-Sig header for signed requests, but log a deprecation warning and prefer Authorization-based signatures. The runtime uses the signature only when Authorization is absent and the incoming request passes a nonce validation check. - SDK updates: TypeScript and Python SDKs updated to prefer Authorization: RedwoodScope when requested by user, and include preflight helpers for browser clients to correctly set the prefetch nonce. - Docs and release notes: added comprehensive docs page and a migration guide (docs/changes/2026-02-20-auth-contract.md). - Tests: added unit and integration tests for header parsing, streaming preflight behavior, and tool auth enforcement. Rollout plan and compatibility: - Backwards compatible: project keys in X-Redwood-Project still work; Authorization bearer tokens unchanged. - Feature flagged rollout: header strictness (reject unknown schemes) gated behind FF:auth.header_strictness. We will enable strictness only after two weeks of telemetry. - Observability: added telemetry keys to surface which header was used for auth and whether the prefetch nonce was seen. Checklist: - [x] Runtime header parser and scope enforcement implemented - [x] OpenAI-compat mapper updated and tested - [x] Streaming preflight/CORS changes (server + ingress templates) - [x] SDK helpers and minor docs updates - [x] Unit and integration test coverage added - [x] Security review (Samir) + perf signoff (Jordan) - [x] Migration docs written Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to header precedence in header_parser.rs and the fallback logic in tool_runner/tool_auth.rs. The earlier implementation accepted any Authorization scheme; this PR documents exact behavior and adds guards to avoid silently ignoring scopes. The opt-in strictness flag allows us to revert to stricter checks quickly if we see breakage in prod. If we decide to accelerate strictness, telemetry surfaces the top callers still using project header fallback.

release_notes: Consolidated auth header semantics across runtime and openai-compat shim: canonical headers (Authorization, X-Redwood-Project, X-Redwood-Org, X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce) introduced, prefetch nonce exposed for SSE and streaming endpoints, RedwoodScope token scheme supported, legacy X-Redwood-Sig accepted with deprecation warning. Backwards compatible; follow migration guide in docs/changes/2026-02-20-auth-contract.md.
